title: Young Modulus, Power and Dynamics
main_stem:
A motor uses a wire to raise a block, as illustrated in Fig. 2.1.

Fig. 2.1 (not to scale)

The base of the block takes a time of $0.49\,\mathrm{s}$ to move vertically upwards from level X to level Y at a constant speed of $0.64\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$. During this time the wire has a strain of $0.0012$. The wire is made of metal of Young modulus $2.2 \times 10^{11}\,\mathrm{Pa}$ and has a uniform cross-section.

The block has a weight of $1.4 \times 10^{4}\,\mathrm{N}$. Assume that the weight of the wire is negligible.

parts.part_stem: The motor has an efficiency of $56\%$.

parts.label: (c)
parts.part_stem: The base of the block now has a uniform deceleration of magnitude $1.3\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$ from level Y until the base of the block stops at level Z.
parts.text: Calculate the tension $T$ in the wire as the base of the block moves from Y to Z.

parts.label: (d)
parts.part_stem: The base of the block is at levels X, Y and Z at times $t_{X}$, $t_{Y}$ and $t_{Z}$ respectively.
parts.text: On Fig. 2.2, sketch a graph to show the variation with time $t$ of the distance $d$ of the base of the block from level X. Numerical values of $d$ and $t$ are not required.
